title: Daweswood House Museum and History Center

services.name: House Tours
services.desc: The Dawes Arboretum is a protected natural haven where everyday adventurers escape the ordinary. Explore the historic Daweswood House Museum, the former country residence of Arboretum cofounders Beman and Bertie Dawes, with a guided tour. With several rooms preserved for accuracy, take a peek into the lives of our founding family. This beautifully preserved historic home offers a glimpse into the lives, values and vision of the Dawes family, allowing you to explore how a private residence grew into a public legacy rooted in nature, generosity and community. A guided tour of Daweswood House invites you to connect more deeply with the history that continues to shape The Arboretum today. Tours

blurb: The Daweswood House Museum was originally the home of the John Brumback family. John, a pioneer blacksmith and farmer, designed and financed the construction of the brick farmhouse in 1867.Around 1917, the Dawes family moved onto the Brumback farm, known at the time Woodland, including the 50-year-old brick farmhouse that became their country home.
